Cfoto | Future Publishing | Getty Images Nvidia rose in extended trading on Tuesday after the embattled chip giant posted beats on the top and bottom lines in the fiscal third quarter. A slate of neocloud stocks, including Nebius and CoreWeave rose on the back of Nvidia's results. The company is a key player in helping neoclouds finance the data center build-out. Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day. 4 Min Ago ZTO Express shares fall over 3% after earnings report Shares for ZTO Express fell over 3% after the logistics company posted its third-quarter earnings report. ZTO reported adjusted net income of 2.571 billion yuan ($383.5 million), up 2.6% from the year-ago period. Revenue for the period came in at 14.361 billion yuan, up 21% from a year earlier. — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Neoclouds rebound following Nvidia's quarterly beat Shares of neocloud companies bounced in extended trading on the back of Nvidia's quarterly report. Iren and CoreWeave each added 4%, while Nebius Group gained about 6%. Nebius in extended trading Tuesday Nvidia plays a key role in financing the artificial intelligence buildout. Neoclouds have been using borrowed funds to construct data centers. -- Darla Mercado 2 Hours Ago Nvidia rises in extended trading following earnings beat Nvidia shares gained about 2% following a better-than-expected earnings report. The AI chip giant earned $2.68 per share on an adjusted basis versus the LSEG consensus estimate for $2.48 per share. Nvidia reported $115.84 billion in revenue, far ahead of the expected $109.10 billion. nvda "Our momentum is real," said Colette Kress, the interim CEO of the company in a statement. — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Dolby Laboratories slips after guidance disappoints Shares of Dolby Laboratories fell about 3% in extended trading after the manufacturer of audio technologies company shared guidance that missed Wall Street's expectations. Dolby Technologies on Tuesday Dolby sees adjusted earnings in a range of $4.27 to $4.42 per share for the fiscal year ending September 2027 on revenue of $1.42 billion. The FactSet consensus sought $4.58 per share and $1.47 billion. Revenue guidance for the current quarter also fell short of expectations. -- Darla Mercado 3 Hours Ago Solar ETF tumbles to lowest level since August 2025 The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) dropped roughly 5% in afternoon trading, sliding to its lowest level since August 2025. The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) on Tuesday The fall also places the ETF on pace for its worst session since June 5, 2026. Enphase Energy, First Solar and SolarEdge dragged the ETF lower, with the three stocks touching at least 52-week lows. The declines occur as the Dec. 4 effective date for President Trump's Section 232 tariffs on solar products approaches. -- Darla Mercado, Gina Francolla 6 Hours Ago Nvidia ticks lower ahead of results Gene Medi | Nurphoto | Getty Images Nvidia shares flipped negative on the day and were last down more than 1% as its quarterly report loomed. The company's third-quarter report , due after Tuesday's market close, comes less than a week after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Nvidia on Tuesday Huang, in his first public statement since leaving the helm, also indicated in a written statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber that he would be willing to come back as CEO. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang said in the statement. -- Darla Mercado, Kif Leswing 6 Hours Ago Software stocks tumble as traders shun tech Software companies were caught up in Tuesday's sell off, with the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) down more than 3% on the day. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) in Tuesday's trading Salesforce plummeted nearly 10%, while cybersecurity play Palo Alto Networks and cloud platform service giant Oracle both lost 4%. Microsoft and Palantir slid 3%. — Darla Mercado 6 Hours Ago SpaceX rises on Bloomberg report that some of its debt could soon go on sale Elon Musk's SpaceX rose Tuesday afternoon following a Bloomberg report that a tranche of the company's $40 billion in debt financing could be sold to investors as early as this week. Bloomberg, which cited people with knowledge of the matter, said that around $4 billion of these bonds could go on the market in the approaching days. SpaceX aims to use this debt sale to cover the cost of artificial intelligence chips, Bloomberg reported. SpaceX was last up almost 3% on the day. SpaceX on Tuesday — Darla Mercado 8 Hours Ago TD Cowen names Coca-Cola top pick for 2027 A Coca-Cola sign is seen in Atlanta on April 15, 2025. Elijah Nouvelage | Afp | Getty Images Shares of Coca-Cola are down a fraction after TD Cowen named the soft drink maker its best idea for 2027, citing pricing power, global reach and Coke's franchise bottling system. TD Cowen reiterated Coke's buy rating and raised its 12-month price target to $112 from $104, implying roughly 13% upside from Monday's close. Coca-Cola is ahead 42% so far in 2026 "The company's international footprint and advantaged franchise bottling system position KO for on-algorithm 5% organic sales growth, well above [consumer packaged goods] peers," said the bank's analyst Robert Moskow. "Despite the stock's rise this year, we think it will move higher as KO proves they can overcome rising inflation and tough comparisons," the analyst wrote Tuesday. — Deena Zaidi 8 Hours Ago Bernstein downgrades PepsiCo, sees 13% downside Illuminated logo for Pepsi on a soda fountain in Walnut Creek, California, March 4, 2026. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Share of PepsiCo were down nearly 2% after Bernstein downgraded the Gatorade and Frito-Lay snack maker to underperform from market-perform. The brokerage and researcher also cut its price target to $128, implying roughly 13% downside from Monday's close, from an earlier $131. Bernstein also cut its 2027 adjusted earnings estimate to $8.27 per share from $8.49. "We forecast a miss on EPS expectations over the next 12 months, driven by underperformance in North America," Bernstein analyst Cristian Rios wrote Tuesday. Pepsi stock price - YTD Rios said North American snack volumes will decline in 2027 as potato and tortilla chip consumption falls, leading Pepsi to continue to lose market share. "Limited pricing power and sustained inflation will eat into productivity savings and pressure margins," the analyst said. — Deena Zaidi 9 Hours Ago Nucor upgraded to overweight with higher price target at Morgan Stanley Charlotte, N.C.-based steelmaker Nucor won an upgrade to overweight from equal weight, and an increased price target of $310 from $300, at Morgan Stanley by analysts led by Carlos De Alba, who said Nucor will benefit from stronger free cash flow as capital investment spending declines. The Wall Street investment bank, which also raised its price target on Steel Dynamics to $270 from $260, lifted its near term steel price forecasts due to tight supplies probably keeping hot rolled coil prices above $1,100 per short ton in the first half of 2027. Nucor shares have soared 57% in 2026 and about 72% over the past year Both Nucor and Steel Dynamics are about 1% higher in early trading Tuesday. — Scott Schnipper 10 Hours Ago JPMorgan downgrades Tyson Foods after sharp rally JPMorgan downgraded Tyson Foods to neutral from overweight, saying its 23% rally over two months leaves limited upside. The bank raised the price target to $65, implying about 2% upside from Monday's close.

headlines.article_text: Apple outage follows Microsoft, FAA and JPMorgan disruptions Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Over four days, outages disrupted Microsoft services, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase transactions and Apple. Security researchers say AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, increasing pressure on organizations to patch systems quickly. "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. In this article MSFT AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 6:25 06:25 DNI Jay Clayton: This is not a cyber attack and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state Closing Bell Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week. "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely." It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt. On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency, and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues . The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal update" as the reason behind its issues. It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days. watch now VIDEO 2:13 02:13 Apple: Many of our systems back up and running after an internal update caused some outages Power Lunch Microsoft 's Outlook issues wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions, and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights. "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life." The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems. Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign. "We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," said Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne. Read more CNBC tech news Anthropic likely to price IPO above the current range of $70 to $78, sources tell CNBC Demis Hassabis’ AI company raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO OpenAI inks agreements with four independent evaluators to boost company’s safety work How Rockstar’s ‘GTA VI’ release could reshape gaming, streaming and even paid time off With the help of artificial intelligence, businesses are patching more software vulnerabilities than ever before and updating archaic systems to prepare for swarms of attacks in the wake of high-profile incidents like Hugging Face. That's leaving information technology and security teams strained and scrambling to keep up with heightened demand, said Sam Rubin, senior vice president of consulting and threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42. Amid this prolonged period of uncertainty, Rubin said businesses should prioritize updating their most exploitable systems and keeping operations underway when an outage hits. "You need to think about how you continue to operate in the face of one of your IT systems going down," he said. Clayton told CNBC that routine upgrades are commonplace at any organization and called for a nationwide digital infrastructure upgrade. Last week, millions of users lost access to email in a fiasco that Microsoft eventually said was the result of an undetected bug that was lurking since July. The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of its system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network. JPMorgan said longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems. Agencies and businesses have ruled out cyberattacks, but the routine patching alibi hasn't satisfied some skeptics, and lawmakers are calling for more transparency. Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., on Tuesday used the recent incidents to make the case for an AI safety bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., acknowledged that it's "too premature" to conclude malicious activity but called for a congressional briefing. "I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America," he said during a press conference on Tuesday. watch now VIDEO 3:41 03:41 NSA says it experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance Power Lunch Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.
